Directions: Read and study the sources about George Washington and early America. Then use the sources to answer each question that follows.
Context: This excerpt is from George Washington’s Rules o Civility (politeness) and Decent (proper) Behavior. The book has more than `100` rules about manners and behavior. When Washington was a young man, he copied the rules from a book that included many of the common manners at the time. Washington used the rules to guide him throughout his life.
Title: Source 1: [Adapted from] George Washington’s Rules of Civility and Decent Behavior
Content: Do not appear to be glad at someone’s failures, even if that person is your enemy.
Those who hold public office are important and should have respect. But office holders should respect their social equals, even if they are private citizens.
Never say anythin rude. Remain moral in ront o everyone.
A man should not value himself too much because he is smart or accomplished. He should not be proud because of his riches or family.
Do not insult those you lead. Do not act bossy.
